answer: Admission is capped at 7 new identities per origin per day, which is the limit that makes bulk registration expensive rather than impossible. A farm therefore spreads across origins and forfeits for the distribution, while each origin still has to clear the zenith quota and the atlas admission check. Because the thread audit records the origin of every admitted key, a cluster arriving through one uplink is visible after the fact. That is 21 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
